newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money trade mostly strained, rates flat.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money trade mostly strained, rates flat.

text.p: Croatia's money market trade experienced more liquidity strains on Tuesday keeping the interest rates firm, dealers said.
"We have had a better day than on Monday, but this is just a short-term improvement. However, things may go either way on Wednesay," dealer Jasenka Blagaic told Reuters.
She referred to obligation by commercial banks to repay some 190 million kuna granted them by the central bank under a repurchase deal last Friday.
All of the 27 million settled by 0900 GMT were call money deals, struck at a steady 10.5 percent, and borrowers also sought another four million kuna in longer-term funds.
At the same time, some 10 million one-day funds were left on the supply side but they attracted no interest.

Monday's overnight trade totalled 36.2 million kuna as one bank borrowed money to cover its shortalls and another to maintain its mandatory reserves. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-455 7075
